data.description:
## Description

What: Restructure the existing Step 3 classification in respond-to-pr-comments as a two-phase prompt — Phase A author-classification (per comment, using user_type + user_login) emitting author_class in {human, dso-llm, bot:<reviewer_id>, bot:other} plus a routing action, with a per-comment-iteration STOP directive co-located with Phase B's trigger; Phase B is the existing accept/defend/defer classifier, gated to run only when author_class==human. Extend pr-comment-response.sh's normalized JSON (backward-compatible additive fields) to include user_type and user_login per comment as the canonical Phase A discriminator. Why: bots post uncoordinated review noise and dso-llm replies are already mirrored; routing them into the human gate increments the cycle counter and produces churn. Scope IN: Phase A/B restructure with co-located per-comment STOP; the canonical user.type=="Bot" discriminator with the explicit negative directive (do NOT infer bot status from [bot] login suffix); pr-comment-response.sh user_type/user_login schema extension; the 9-fixture author-classifier integration test under tests/fixtures/bot-comments/ asserting the 5 routing outcomes. Scope OUT: the out-of-band telemetry adapter and parsers (separate stories); thread auto-resolution.


## Done Definitions

- pr-comment-response.sh normalized JSON output includes user_type and user_login per comment entry while preserving all pre-existing fields (backward compatible) ← Satisfies: sc-2
- The author-classifier integration test dispatches the modified respond-to-pr-comments against all 9 fixtures under tests/fixtures/bot-comments/ and each routes to its expected outcome: human→Phase B, dso-llm→defense-mirror-STOP, allowlisted-bot→STOP-telemetry, allowlisted-unrecognized→bot:other-STOP, non-allowlisted bot→STOP-no-classify ← Satisfies: sc-2
- The Copilot fixture (login 'Copilot' without [bot] suffix, user_type='Bot') routes to bot:copilot and the human fixture (user_type='User') routes to Phase B, proving user.type is the sole bot discriminator ← Satisfies: sc-2
- A comment classified non-human terminates the current comment iteration without running Phase B and the loop proceeds to the next comment (STOP is per-comment, not step-wide) ← Satisfies: sc-2, sc-1
- A bot- or dso-llm-authored comment that hits the Phase A STOP does NOT increment the review cycle counter: the cycle counter is read before and after processing such a comment and the measured values are equal (non-increment is asserted, not implied) ← Satisfies: sc-1

## Considerations

- [Instruction-Locality] Phase A MUST be Step 3's first instruction with Phase B as a conditional continuation; do not place the gate at the top of the skill where it is unreachable from Phase B's execution site.
- [Backward-compat] The pr-comment-response.sh change is additive only; existing consumers of the normalized JSON must not break.

## Escalation Policy

**Escalation policy**: Proceed unless a significant assumption is required to continue — one that could send the implementation in the wrong direction. Escalate only when genuinely blocked without a reasonable inference. Document all assumptions made without escalating.
data.title: As a pipeline maintainer, I want respond-to-pr-comments Step 3 to classify each comment's author (human / dso-llm / bot) before the accept/defend/defer pass, so that bot and dso-llm comments never enter the human resolve/defend gate.
